column1: # Published neighbour, parent and child known answers for S2CellId.
# Every row here is transcribed from a named primary source.  Nothing was
# computed, and nothing was generalised past what a source actually states.
#       The edge neighbours of the level-0 face cell are four face cells with
#       these face numbers, in this order.  Source B publishes exactly one such
#       row, for face 1 (lines 574-580); no other face's list is published, so
#       The multiset of all neighbours of <cell> at its own level, in the
#       "face/childpos" debug spelling.  Source C lists these with
#       UnorderedElementsAre, so order is irrelevant and a repeat counts twice:
#       the 3/0000 row really does contain 2/3333 twice and upstream expects it.
#       Source B, lines 610-617: for the leaf cell
#       comment there as "the corner of faces 0, 4, and 5", the vertex
#       neighbours at level 0 are exactly the three face cells with the listed
#       face numbers, sorted.  The cell is named by the arguments upstream passes
#       to FromFacePosLevel, so the row cannot be misread as a different cell.
#       under the comment "Level-0 cell (i.e. face) centered at (0, 0)".  With
#       source D, lines 90-95, which requires the leaf cell of (0, 0) to be on
#       face 0, this pins the projection origin: the level-0 cell of face 0 has
#       id 0x1000000000000000 and its centre is exactly (0, 0).
#       Source F, lines 99-138, whose four cells are commented "Pittsburg".
#       Source G, lines 47-97.  It builds CellIDFromFacePosLevel(3, 0x12345678,
#       MaxLevel-4) and asserts the cell's position after that masking, the
#       position of the first child, of the first grandchild, of the immediate
#       parent and of the grandparent, and the level.
